modern: This gracious word came true once at our glorious Lord’s first coming, and is still to be fulfilled more completely at his second coming, but it’s also for daily use. Is it dark for you, reader? Is the night deepening into thicker blackness? Still, let’s not despair: the sun will rise. When the night is darkest, the dawn is nearest.

The sun that will rise is no ordinary one. It is THE Sun, the Sun of Righteousness, every ray of which is holiness. He who comes to cheer us comes by the way of justice as well as mercy. He comes to break no law, even to save us. Jesus shows God’s holiness as much as his love. Our rescue, when it comes, will be safe, because it will be right.

The one question we need to ask is, “Do we fear the name of the Lord? Do we revere the living God and walk in his ways?” If we do, then for us the night must be short. And when the morning comes, all the sickness and sorrow of our soul will be over forever. Light, warmth, joy and clear sight will come, and healing of every disease and distress will follow.
Has Jesus risen on us? Let’s sit in the sun. Has he hidden his face? Let’s wait for him to rise. He’ll shine out as surely as the sun.

notes.note: A name for Christ, from the day’s text ([[Mal.4.2|Malachi 4:2]]).
A coming or arrival. His second advent is his return.
The sun’s rays pictured as wings spreading healing.
Hold God in loving awe and reverence, not terror.
Treat with deep respect and awe.

modern: Yes, when the sun shines, the sick leave their rooms and go out to breathe the fresh air. When the sun brings spring and summer, the cattle leave their stalls and look for pasture high up in the Alps. In the same way, when we’re aware of our fellowship with our Lord, we leave the stall of gloom and walk out in the fields of holy confidence. We climb the mountains of joy and feed on sweet pasture that grows nearer heaven than the fodder of worldly people.

To “go forth” and to “grow up” is a double promise. My soul, be eager to enjoy both blessings! Why should you be a prisoner? Get up and walk in freedom. Jesus says his sheep will go in and out and find pasture. So go out and feed in the rich meadows of boundless love.

Why stay a baby in grace? Grow up. Young calves grow fast, especially if they’re fed in the stall, and you have the choicest care of your Redeemer. So grow in grace, and in the knowledge of your Lord and Savior. Don’t be cramped or stunted. The Sun of Righteousness has risen on you. Respond to his rays the way buds respond to the sun in the sky. Open your heart, spread out and grow up into him in all things.

notes.note: Calves kept in the stall and well fed, which grow fast and frisk about when they’re let out.
Feeling low and discouraged.
Animal feed, fodder.
Of the flesh: the desires of our fallen human nature, not only sexual ones.

notes.term: Go in and out and find pasture

notes.note: “Grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ” ([[2Pet.3.18|2 Peter 3:18]]).
Cramped, held back.

notes.term: Grow up into Him in all things
notes.note: [[Eph.4.15|Ephesians 4:15]].

modern: If this isn’t a promise in form, it is in fact. Indeed, it’s more than one promise: it’s a whole cluster of promises. It’s a mass of rubies and emeralds and diamonds set in a nugget of gold. It’s a question that can never be answered in a way that would worry our hearts. What can the Lord refuse us after giving us Jesus? If we need everything in heaven and on earth, he’ll give it to us, because if there had been a limit anywhere, he would have held back his own Son.

What do I need today? I only have to ask for it. I can ask earnestly, but not as if I had to apply pressure and squeeze an unwilling gift out of the Lord’s hand, because he will give freely. Of his own free will he gave us his own Son. Certainly no one would have suggested such a gift to him. No one would have dared to ask for it; it would have been far too presumptuous. He freely gave his only Son. So, my soul, can’t you trust your heavenly Father to give you anything, to give you everything? Your poor prayer would have no force with the Almighty if force were needed. But his love, like a spring, rises by itself and overflows to supply all your needs.

notes.note: A mass of different pieces stuck together, like a rock full of pebbles.
Force out, squeeze out.
Too bold; taking far too much for granted.
God’s one and only Son ([[John.3.16|John 3:16]]).
Being all-powerful; here, God himself.

modern: He has left us, and yet we aren’t left orphans. He is our comfort, and he has gone, but we aren’t comfortless. Our comfort is that he will come to us, and that’s comfort enough to keep us going through his long absence. Jesus is already on his way. He says, “I come quickly”: he is riding toward us at full speed. He says, “I will come,” and no one can stop his coming or put it off for a quarter of an hour. He says especially, “I will come to you,” and so he will. His coming is especially to and for his own people. This is meant to comfort them now, while they grieve that the Bridegroom hasn’t appeared yet.

When we lose the joyful sense of his presence, we grieve, but we mustn’t grieve as if there were no hope. In a little anger our Lord has hidden himself from us for a moment, but he’ll come back in full favor. He leaves us in one sense, but only in one sense. When he withdraws, he leaves a pledge behind that he’ll come back. O Lord, come quickly! There’s no life in this earthly existence if you’re gone. We long for the return of your sweet smile. When will you come to us? We’re sure you will appear, but be like a gazelle or a young deer. Don’t delay, our God!

notes.note: The Greek word means “orphans,” which is why Spurgeon says we aren’t left orphans.
[[Rev.22.20|Revelation 22:20]].
At top speed, like a mail rider changing horses at every post.
Christ, coming for his bride, the church ([[Matt.25.6|Matthew 25:6]]).

notes.term: Sorrow as if there were no hope
notes.note: “That ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope” ([[1Thess.4.13|1 Thessalonians 4:13]]).
“In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment; but with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee” ([[Isa.54.8|Isaiah 54:8]]).

notes.term: Like a roe, or a young hart
notes.note: Swift like a gazelle or a young deer: the bride’s call to her beloved in [[Song.8.14|Song of Solomon 8:14]].
Don’t delay ([[Ps.40.17|Psalm 40:17]]).

modern: My own sight of the precious blood is for my comfort, but it’s the Lord’s sight of it that makes me safe. Even when I can’t see it, the Lord looks at it and passes over me because of it. If I’m not as much at peace as I ought to be because my faith is dim, I’m still just as safe, because the Lord’s eye isn’t dim, and he looks steadily at the blood of the great Sacrifice. What a joy this is!

The Lord sees the deep inner meaning, the infinite fullness of all that the death of his dear Son means. He sees it with the restful memory of justice satisfied and all his matchless qualities glorified. He watched creation as it went forward and said, “It is very good.” But what does he say about redemption in its completeness? What does he say about the obedience of his dearly loved Son, even to death? No one can describe his delight in Jesus, his rest in the sweet fragrance of Jesus’ offering when he gave himself without blemish to God.

So now let’s rest in calm security. We have God’s Sacrifice and God’s Word to give us a sense of perfect security. He will, he must, pass over us, because he didn’t spare our glorious Substitute. Justice joins hands with love to provide everlasting salvation for all who are sprinkled with the blood.

notes.note: On the night of the first Passover, the Lord passed over every house marked with a lamb’s blood ([[Exod.12.13|Exodus 12:13]]).
God’s justice requires sin to be punished. In Christ’s death that demand was fully met, or “satisfied.”
God’s qualities, such as his justice, love and wisdom.
[[Gen.1.31|Genesis 1:31]].
“He humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross” ([[Phil.2.8|Philippians 2:8]]).
A pleasing fragrance, as of an acceptable sacrifice. Christ “hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour” ([[Eph.5.2|Ephesians 5:2]]).
“Who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God” ([[Heb.9.14|Hebrews 9:14]]).
Someone who takes another’s place. Christ took the punishment our sins deserved.

modern: The city is full of worries, and anyone who has to go there day after day finds it wears them down badly. It’s full of noise and rush and bustle and hard toil, with plenty of temptations, losses and worries. But going there with God’s blessing takes the edge off its difficulty. Staying there with that blessing means finding pleasure in its duties and strength to match its demands.

A blessing in the city may not make us great, but it will keep us good. It may not make us rich, but it will keep us honest. Whether we’re porters or clerks, managers or merchants or magistrates, the city will give us chances to be useful. It’s good fishing where there are schools of fish, and there’s hope in working for our Lord among the crowds. We might prefer the quiet of country life, but if we’re called to the city, we can certainly prefer it, because there’s room there for our energies.

Today let’s expect good things because of this promise, and let’s take care to have an open ear for the voice of the Lord and a ready hand to do what he says. Obedience brings the blessing. “In keeping his commandments there is great reward.”

notes.note: Listen and obey.
Hard labor, toil.
Men who carried goods and luggage for a living.
Local judges and officials.
Large schools of fish.

notes.term: “In keeping his commandments there is great reward”
notes.note: From [[Ps.19.11|Psalm 19:11]], “in keeping of them there is great reward.”

modern: In these words Eliphaz spoke a great truth, one that sums up many an inspired Scripture. Reader, has sin pulled you down? Have you become like a ruin? Has the hand of the Lord gone out against you, so that you’ve been made poor in your circumstances and broken in spirit? Was it your own foolishness that brought all this ruin on you? Then the first thing to do is to come back to the Lord. With deep repentance and sincere faith, find your way back from your backsliding. It’s your duty, because you’ve turned away from the One you claimed to serve. It’s your wisdom, because you can’t fight him and prosper. And it’s your urgent need, because what he has done is nothing compared with what he may do to discipline you, since he is Almighty to punish.

Look at the promise that invites you! You will be “built up.” No one but the Almighty can set up the fallen pillars and restore the tottering walls of your condition, but he can and he will do it if you come back to him. Don’t delay. Your crushed mind may give way completely if you go on rebelling, but heartfelt confession will ease you, and humble faith will comfort you. Do this, and all will be well.

notes.note: One of Job’s three friends. God later said they hadn’t spoken rightly of him ([[Job.42.7|Job 42:7]]), but this saying agrees with the rest of Scripture.
Your circumstances and property.
Ruin; falling to pieces.
Slipping back from following God.
Claimed publicly.
Discipline, correction.

modern: Fear of falling is healthy. Being reckless is no sign of wisdom. There are times when we feel we must go down unless we have very special support. Here it is. God’s right hand is a grand thing to lean on. Notice, it isn’t only his hand, though that keeps heaven and earth in their places, but his *right* hand: his power joined with skill, his power where it is most expert. And that isn’t all. It’s written, “I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.” The hand he uses to uphold his holiness and carry out his royal sentences will be stretched out to hold up those who trust him. Our danger is frightening, but our security is joyful. Devils can’t throw down the one God holds up.

Our feet may be weak, but God’s right hand is almighty. The road may be rough, but the Almighty holds us up. We can go forward boldly. We won’t fall. Let’s lean always where everything leans. God won’t take his strength away, because his righteousness is in it too. He’ll be faithful to his promise and faithful to his Son, and so faithful to us. How happy we ought to be! And aren’t we?

notes.note: Reckless, daring.
The hand of strength and skill. In the Bible, God’s right hand stands for his power in action ([[Exod.15.6|Exodus 15:6]]).
Skillful with the hands. The word comes from the Latin for “right hand.”
Hold up, support.
Being all-powerful; here, God himself.

modern: Grace turns us into precious metal, and then the fire and the furnace follow as a matter of course. Does that startle us? Would we rather be counted worthless, so we could lie at rest like the stones of the field? That would be choosing the lower part, like Esau, taking the stew and giving up the covenant inheritance. No, Lord, we’ll gladly be thrown into the furnace rather than be thrown out of your presence!

The fire only refines; it doesn’t destroy. We’re to be brought through the fire, not left in it. The Lord values his people like silver, and so he takes pains to purge away their dross. If we’re wise, we’ll welcome the refining rather than refuse it. We’ll pray to have our impurities taken out of us rather than to be taken out of the melting pot.

O Lord, you test us indeed! We’re ready to melt in the fierceness of the flame. Still, this is your way, and your way is best. Hold us up through the trial and finish the work of purifying us, and we’ll be yours forever and ever.

notes.note: Changes from one substance into another.
In Zechariah’s prophecy, the part of the people God brings through the fire and keeps as his own ([[Zech.13.8-Zech.13.9|Zechariah 13:8–9]]).
Esau sold his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of stew ([[Gen.25.33-Gen.25.34|Genesis 25:33–34]]).
Lower, more worthless.
A share of an inheritance.
The scum of impurities skimmed off when metal is melted.
A cheaper metal mixed into a precious one.
A pot for melting metal in a furnace.

modern: Paul was chosen to see the Lord and hear him speak from heaven. This divine choice was a high privilege for Paul himself, but it wasn’t meant to stop with him. It was meant to reach others, yes, all people. It’s to Paul that Europe owes the gospel to this day.

It’s our part, in our own measure, to be witnesses of what the Lord has revealed to us, and we hide that precious revelation at our peril. First we must see and hear, or we’ll have nothing to tell. But once we have, we must be eager to give our testimony. It must be personal: “Thou shalt be.” It must be for Christ: “Thou shalt be his witness.” It must be constant and all-absorbing. We’re to be this above everything else, and to the exclusion of many other things. Our witness mustn’t be only to a select few who will welcome us gladly, but “to all men”: to everyone we can reach, young or old, rich or poor, good or bad. We must never be silent like people possessed by a mute spirit, because the text before us is a command and a promise, and we mustn’t miss it: “Thou shalt be his witness.” “Ye are my witnesses, saith the Lord.”
Lord, make this word come true for me too!

notes.note: Ananias’s words to Paul after he was blinded on the Damascus road ([[Acts.22.14-Acts.22.15|Acts 22:14–15]]).
Choice. God chose Paul for this work.
Paul first preached in Europe at Philippi, after a vision of a man of Macedonia calling for help ([[Acts.16.9-Acts.16.10|Acts 16:9–10]]).
A spirit that made a person unable to speak ([[Mark.9.17|Mark 9:17]]). “Dumb” meant mute.

modern: Our dear children don’t have the Spirit of God by nature, as we can plainly see. We see much in them that makes us afraid for their future, and this drives us to agonizing prayer. When a son becomes especially stubborn, we cry with Abraham, “Oh, that Ishmael might live before thee!” We’d rather see our daughters be Hannahs than empresses. This verse should greatly encourage us. It follows the words, “Fear not, O Jacob, my servant,” and it may well banish our fears.

The Lord will give his Spirit. He’ll give it plentifully, pouring it out. He’ll give it effectively, so that it will be a real and eternal blessing. Under this divine outpouring our children will come forward, and “one shall say, I am the Lord’s; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob.”

This is one of the promises the Lord wants to be asked about. Shouldn’t we pray for our children at set times and in a definite way? We can’t give them new hearts, but the Holy Spirit can, and he is easily persuaded. The great Father takes pleasure in the prayers of fathers and mothers. Do we have any loved ones still outside the ark? Let’s not rest until they’re shut in with us by the Lord’s own hand.

notes.note: Stubborn, set on going wrong.

notes.term: “Oh, that Ishmael might live before thee!”
notes.note: Abraham’s prayer for his son ([[Gen.17.18|Genesis 17:18]]).
Women of prayer like Hannah, the mother of Samuel ([[1Sam.1.10-1Sam.1.11|1 Samuel 1:10–11]]).
Effectively; actually doing what it sets out to do.

notes.term: “One shall say, I am the Lord’s”

notes.note: “I will yet for this be enquired of by the house of Israel, to do it for them” ([[Ezek.36.37|Ezekiel 36:37]]): God wants to be asked for what he has promised.
Pleaded with, persuaded.
Outside safety, like those left out of Noah’s ark, which God himself shut ([[Gen.7.16|Genesis 7:16]]).

modern: A special blessing for a memorable occasion. Abram had settled a family quarrel. He had said, “Let there be no strife, I pray thee, between thee and me, for we be brethren,” and so he received the blessing that belongs to peacemakers. The Lord, the giver of peace, loves to show his grace to those who seek peace and pursue it. If we want closer fellowship with God, we must keep closer to the ways of peace.

Abram had treated his relative very generously, giving him the choice of the land. If we give things up for the sake of peace, the Lord will more than make it up to us. As far as the patriarch could see, he could claim, and we can do the same by faith. Abram had to wait to actually possess it, but the Lord settled the land on him and his descendants for good. Boundless blessings belong to us as a covenant gift. All things are ours. When we please the Lord, he makes us look in every direction and see everything as our own. Whether things present or things to come, all are ours, and we are Christ’s, and Christ is God’s.

notes.term: After that Lot was separated from him
notes.note: Abram’s and Lot’s herdsmen quarreled, so Abram let his nephew choose where to go, and Lot chose the well-watered plain near Sodom ([[Gen.13.8-Gen.13.11|Genesis 13:8–11]]).
“Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God” ([[Matt.5.9|Matthew 5:9]]).
Close fellowship and sharing, with God or with each other.
A relative, especially one with the right and duty to rescue family (as Boaz did for Ruth).
Abraham. A patriarch is the father and head of a family or tribe in early Bible times.
An old legal term for an estate fixed to pass down a family line, which could never be sold off or taken away.
Descendants.
“All are yours; and ye are Christ’s; and Christ is God’s” ([[1Cor.3.21-1Cor.3.23|1 Corinthians 3:21–23]]).

modern: Isaac was blessed like this when he walked out in the field in the evening to meditate. How often the Lord has met us when we’ve been alone! The hedges and the trees can bear witness to our joy. We look for blessing like that again.

Boaz was blessed like this when he reaped his harvest and his workers greeted him with blessings. May the Lord prosper everyone who drives a plow! Every farmer can hold God to this promise, as long as he really obeys the voice of the Lord God.
We go to the field to work, as father Adam did. And since the curse fell on the ground through the sin of the first Adam, it’s a great comfort to find a blessing through the second Adam.
We go to the field for exercise, and we’re happy in the belief that the Lord will bless that exercise and give us health, which we’ll use for his glory.
We go to the field to study nature, and there’s nothing in the knowledge of the visible creation that God’s blessing can’t make holy for the highest uses.
In the end we have to go to the field to bury our dead. Yes, others will in turn carry us to God’s acre. But we’re blessed, whether we’re weeping at the grave or sleeping in it.

notes.note: “Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide” ([[Gen.24.63|Genesis 24:63]]).
When Boaz came to his reapers he said, “The LORD be with you,” and they answered, “The LORD bless thee” ([[Ruth.2.4|Ruth 2:4]]).
Blessings.
Plead it in prayer.

notes.term: The curse fell on the soil
notes.note: “Cursed is the ground for thy sake” ([[Gen.3.17|Genesis 3:17]]).
Christ, “the last Adam” ([[1Cor.15.45|1 Corinthians 15:45]]).
Made holy; set apart for God.
An old name for a churchyard or cemetery.

modern: What a lovely reward for trust! My Lord, give it to me in full! The person who trusts, more than anyone, feels they’re a sinner, and look: mercy is ready for them. They know they deserve nothing, but mercy comes in and keeps house for them generously. O Lord, give me this mercy, just as I trust in you!

Look, my soul, what a bodyguard you have! As a prince is surrounded by soldiers, so you’re surrounded by mercy. In front and behind and on every side ride these mounted guards of grace. We live at the very center of the system of mercy, because we live in Christ Jesus.

My soul, what an atmosphere you breathe! As the air surrounds you, so does your Lord’s mercy. The wicked have many sorrows, but you have so many mercies that your sorrows aren’t worth mentioning. David says, “Be glad in the Lord, and rejoice, ye righteous; and shout for joy, all ye that are upright in heart.” In obedience to this command, my heart will triumph in God, and I’ll tell out my gladness. As you’ve surrounded me with mercy, I’ll surround your altars, my God, with songs of thanks!

notes.note: Surround.
Generous.
Soldiers.

notes.term: To the wicked there are many sorrows
notes.note: From the first half of the day’s verse, “Many sorrows shall be to the wicked” ([[Ps.32.10|Psalm 32:10]]).
[[Ps.32.11|Psalm 32:11]], the next verse.
“So will I compass thine altar, O LORD: that I may publish with the voice of thanksgiving” ([[Ps.26.6-Ps.26.7|Psalm 26:6–7]]).

modern: I can put my seal to that first sentence. Can’t you? Yes, the Lord has thought of us, provided for us, comforted us, rescued us and guided us. In all the workings of his providence he has been mindful of us, never overlooking our small affairs. His mind has been full of us; that’s the other way of putting the word “mindful.” It has been like this all along, without a single break. At special times, though, we’ve seen this mindfulness more clearly, and we’d like to recall those times now with overflowing gratitude. Yes, yes, “the Lord hath been mindful of us.”

The next sentence follows logically from the first. Since God doesn’t change, he’ll keep on being mindful of us in the future as he has been in the past, and his being mindful of us amounts to blessing us. But here we have not only the conclusion of reason, but the statement of inspiration. We have it on the Holy Spirit’s authority: “HE WILL BLESS US.” This means great things, things past finding out. The very vagueness of the promise shows its infinite reach. He’ll bless us in his own divine way, and that forever and ever. So let’s each say, “Bless the Lord, O my soul!”

notes.note: Put my stamp of agreement on; confirm.
Keeping in mind; paying attention to.
Humble, small (not unkind).
Equal in effect; as good as.
Too great to be fully searched out ([[Job.5.9|Job 5:9]]).

modern: This is how the Lord makes known his sparing mercies. It may be, reader, that you’re under heavy displeasure right now, and everything threatens your swift ruin. Let this text hold you back from despair. The Lord is inviting you now to think about your ways and confess your sins. If he had been a man, he would have cut you off long ago. If he acted now the way people do, it would be a word and a blow, and that would be the end of you. But it isn’t like that, for “as high as the heavens are above the earth, so high are his ways above your ways.”

You’re right to think he is angry, but he doesn’t keep his anger forever. If you turn from sin to Jesus, God will turn from his anger. Because God is God and not man, there’s still forgiveness for you, even if you’re steeped up to your neck in sin. You have God to deal with, not a hard man, or even a man who is merely just. No human being could have patience with you. You would have worn out an angel, as you’ve worn out your grieving father. But God is patient. Come and try him right now. Confess, believe and turn from your evil way, and you’ll be saved.

notes.note: The leading tribe of the northern kingdom of Israel; here, the whole rebellious nation God still loved ([[Hos.11.8|Hosea 11:8]]).
Mercies that hold back punishment.
An old saying for striking without waiting to listen.
Spurgeon’s wording of [[Isa.55.9|Isaiah 55:9]], “as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways.”

notes.term: He keepeth not His anger for ever
notes.note: “He retaineth not his anger for ever, because he delighteth in mercy” ([[Mic.7.18|Micah 7:18]]).
Sin, wickedness.
Patient; slow to anger.

modern: God had done great things for King Asa and Judah, yet they were a weak people. Their feet tottered badly in the ways of the Lord, and their hearts wavered, so they had to be warned that the Lord would be with them while they were with him, but that if they left him, he would leave them. They were also reminded of their sister kingdom: how badly it had gone for it in its rebellion, and how gracious the Lord had been to it when it repented. The Lord’s aim was to settle them in his way and make them strong in righteousness. That’s how it ought to be with us too. God deserves to be served with all the energy we’re capable of.

If the service of God is worth anything, it’s worth everything. We’ll find our best reward in the Lord’s work if we do it with determined effort. Our work isn’t in vain in the Lord, and we know it. Halfhearted work will bring no reward, but when we throw our whole soul into the cause, we’ll see it prosper. This text was sent to the writer of these notes on a day of terrible storm, and it told him to put on full steam, sure of reaching port safely with a glorious cargo.

notes.note: A good king of Judah. The prophet Azariah met him after a great victory and spoke these words ([[2Chr.15.1-2Chr.15.2|2 Chronicles 15:1–2]]).
The northern kingdom of Israel, which had broken away from Judah ([[2Chr.15.3-2Chr.15.4|2 Chronicles 15:3–4]]).

notes.term: Our labor is not in vain in the Lord
notes.note: [[1Cor.15.58|1 Corinthians 15:58]].
Spurgeon himself.
Cargo.

modern: His own Spirit has worked this desire in us, so he’ll answer it. It’s his own life within us that prompts the cry, so he’ll hear it. Those who fear him are people under the holiest influence, so their desire is to glorify God and enjoy him forever. Like Daniel, they’re people of desires, and the Lord will make their longings come true.

Holy desires are grace in the green shoot, and the heavenly Farmer will tend them until they become full grain in the ear. God-fearing people want to be holy, to be useful, to be a blessing to others, and so to honor their Lord. They want supplies for their needs, help under their burdens, guidance when they’re puzzled and rescue when they’re in distress. Sometimes this desire is so strong, and their case so urgent, that they cry out in agony like little children in pain. And then the Lord works most completely and does everything that’s needed, as this Word says: “and will save them.”
Yes, if we fear God, we have nothing else to fear. If we cry to the Lord, our salvation is certain.
Reader, put this text on your tongue and keep it in your mouth all day, and it will be like “a wafer made with honey” to you.

notes.note: Worked.

notes.term: Glorify God, and enjoy Him for ever
notes.note: From the Westminster Shorter Catechism: “Man’s chief end is to glorify God, and to enjoy him for ever.”
The angel called Daniel “greatly beloved,” literally “a man of desires” ([[Dan.9.23|Daniel 9:23]]).
From Jesus’ parable of the growing seed: “first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear” ([[Mark.4.28|Mark 4:28]]).
Farmer.
Confusion; being at a loss.
Completely, covering everything.
The taste of manna ([[Exod.16.31|Exodus 16:31]]).

modern: There’s a limit to affliction. God sends it and God takes it away. Do you sigh and say, “When will the end be?” Remember that our griefs will surely and finally end when this poor earthly life is over. Let’s wait quietly and patiently bear the Lord’s will until he comes.

Meanwhile, our Father in heaven takes away the rod once it has fully done what he meant it to do. When he has whipped our foolishness out of us, there’ll be no more strokes. Or if the trouble was sent to test us, so that our graces could bring glory to God, it will end when the Lord has made us testify to his praise. We wouldn’t want the trouble to leave until God has drawn out of us all the honor we can possibly give him.

There may be “a great calm” today. Who knows how soon those raging waves will give way to a sea of glass, with seabirds sitting on the gentle swell? After long tribulation the flail is hung up and the wheat rests in the barn. Before many hours have passed, we may be just as happy as we’re sorrowful now. It isn’t hard for the Lord to turn night into day. The One who sends the clouds can clear the skies just as easily. Let’s take heart. It’s better farther on. Let’s sing hallelujah ahead of time.

notes.note: God’s discipline, the way a father corrects a child.
When Jesus rebuked the wind and the sea, “there was a great calm” ([[Matt.8.26|Matthew 8:26]]).
Perfectly smooth water, like the sea of glass before God’s throne ([[Rev.4.6|Revelation 4:6]]).
Trouble, suffering. The word comes from the Latin for a threshing board, which is why Spurgeon thinks of the flail.
A tool for beating grain to separate it from the husk.
A barn for storing grain.
Ahead of time.

modern: What’s the matter with you? Have you lost your way? Are you tangled in a dark wood, unable to find your path? Stand still and see the salvation of God. He knows the way, and he’ll lead you in it if you cry to him.

Every day brings its own puzzles. How sweet to feel that the Lord’s guidance is continual! If we choose our own way, or ask advice from flesh and blood, we throw off the Lord’s guidance. But if we hold back from self-will, he’ll direct every step of our road, every hour of the day, every day of the year and every year of our life. If we’ll only be guided, we’ll be guided. If we commit our way to the Lord, he’ll direct our course so that we won’t get lost.

But notice who this promise is made to. Read the verse before: “If thou draw out thy soul to the hungry.” We must feel for others and give them, not a few dry crusts, but the kind of things we’d want to receive ourselves. If we show tender care for our fellow human beings in their hour of need, then the Lord will look after our needs and make himself our continual Guide. Jesus is the Leader, not of misers or of those who oppress the poor, but of the kind and tenderhearted. People like that are pilgrims who will never miss their way.

notes.note: What’s wrong with you?

notes.term: Stand still, and see the salvation of God
notes.note: Moses to Israel at the Red Sea: “Stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD” ([[Exod.14.13|Exodus 14:13]]).
Mere human beings. After his conversion Paul “conferred not with flesh and blood” ([[Gal.1.16|Galatians 1:16]]).

notes.term: Commit our way unto the Lord
notes.note: “Commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass” ([[Ps.37.5|Psalm 37:5]]).

notes.term: Draw out thy soul to the hungry
notes.note: Pour yourself out for the hungry ([[Isa.58.10|Isaiah 58:10]]).

modern: This is a cheering word for those of humble position and modest means. Our God takes very gracious notice of those with small property, small talent, small influence, small weight. God cares for the small things in creation, and even notices sparrows landing on the ground. Nothing is small to God, because he uses insignificant agents to carry out his purposes. Let the least of people ask God for a blessing on their littleness, and they’ll find their narrow little world a happy one.

Among those who fear the Lord, there are little ones and great ones. Some are babies and some are giants. But they’re all blessed. Little faith is blessed faith. Trembling hope is blessed hope. Every grace of the Holy Spirit, even if it’s only in bud, carries a blessing inside it. What’s more, the Lord Jesus bought both the small and the great with the same precious blood, and he has promised to keep the lambs as well as the full-grown sheep. No mother overlooks her child because it’s little. No, the smaller it is, the more tenderly she nurses it. If the Lord has any preference, he doesn’t list them as “great and small,” but as “small and great.”

notes.note: Position in society, and property.
Humble, poor (not unkind).

notes.term: Sparrows in their lighting upon the ground
notes.note: “One of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father” ([[Matt.10.29|Matthew 10:29]]).
A small, narrow area of life.

notes.term: The lambs as well as the full-grown sheep
notes.note: “He shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom” ([[Isa.40.11|Isaiah 40:11]]).
Promised; committed himself.

modern: This isn’t a promise if we look only at the words, but it truly is one in its meaning, because David spoke a word the Lord backed by making it come true. He reasoned from past rescues that he would get help in a new danger. In Jesus all the promises are “Yea and Amen” to the glory of God through us, and so the Lord’s past dealings with his believing people will be repeated.

So come, let’s remember the Lord’s past lovingkindnesses. We couldn’t have hoped to be rescued before by our own strength, yet the Lord rescued us. Won’t he save us again? We’re sure he will. As David ran to meet his enemy, so will we. The Lord has been with us, he is with us, and he has said, “I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.” Why do we tremble? Was the past a dream? Think of the dead bear and lion. Who is this Philistine? True, he isn’t quite the same; he’s neither bear nor lion. But God is the same, and his honor is as much at stake in the one case as in the other. He didn’t save us from the beasts of the forest to let a giant kill us. Let’s take courage.

notes.note: Goliath, the giant David went out to fight.
Backed up, confirmed.
“All the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of God by us” ([[2Cor.1.20|2 Corinthians 1:20]]).
Before, in the past.

notes.term: As David ran to meet his foe
notes.note: “David hasted, and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine” ([[1Sam.17.48|1 Samuel 17:48]]).
[[Heb.13.5|Hebrews 13:5]].

modern: We must, of course, be in Christ to live for him, and we must remain in him to be able to claim the generous gift of this promise. To remain in Jesus is never to leave him for another love or another aim, but to stay in a living, loving, conscious, willing union with him. The branch isn’t only always near the trunk; it’s always drawing life and fruitfulness from it. In one sense all true believers remain in Christ. But there’s a higher meaning, and we must know it before we can have unlimited power at the throne. “Ask what ye will” is for Enochs who walk with God, for Johns who lean on the Lord’s chest, for those whose union with Christ leads to constant fellowship.

The heart must remain in love, the mind must be rooted in faith, our hope must be cemented to the Word, and the whole person must be joined to the Lord. Otherwise it would be dangerous to trust us with power in prayer. A blank check can only be given to someone whose very life is, “Not I, but Christ liveth in me.” You who break off your fellowship, what power you lose! If you want to be mighty in your pleading, the Lord himself must remain in you, and you in him.

notes.note: Remain, stay, live in.
Generous gifts.
“Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him” ([[Gen.5.24|Genesis 5:24]]).

notes.term: Johns who lie in the Lord’s bosom
notes.note: At the Last Supper John leaned against Jesus’ chest ([[John.13.23|John 13:23]]).
Close fellowship and sharing, with God or with each other.
French for “blank paper”: a signed blank check, full freedom to ask anything.

notes.term: “Not I, but Christ liveth in me”
notes.note: From [[Gal.2.20|Galatians 2:20]].

modern: Notice carefully that we must hear Jesus speak if we expect him to hear us speak. If we have no ear for Christ, he’ll have no ear for us. As much as we hear, so much will we be heard.

What’s more, what we hear must stay with us, must live in us and must remain in our character as a force and a power. We must take in the truths Jesus taught, the commands he gave and the movements of his Spirit within us, or we’ll have no power at the mercy seat.

Suppose we have taken in our Lord’s words and they remain in us. What a boundless field of privilege opens up! We’re to have our will in prayer, because we’ve already surrendered our will to the Lord’s command. This is how Elijahs are trained to handle the keys of heaven, and to lock or unlock the clouds. One such person is worth a thousand ordinary Christians. Do we humbly want to be intercessors for the church and the world, and like Luther to be able to have what we will from the Lord? Then we must bend our ear to the voice of the Well-beloved, treasure his words and carefully obey them. Whoever wants to pray effectively needs to “hearken diligently.”

notes.note: Commands, instructions.
The gold lid of the ark of the covenant, where God met with his people; a picture of coming to God in prayer.

notes.term: Elijahs… lock or loose the clouds
notes.note: Elijah prayed and it didn’t rain for three and a half years; he prayed again and it rained ([[Jas.5.17-Jas.5.18|James 5:17–18]]).
People who pray for others.
Martin Luther (1483–1546), the German reformer, famous for bold and persistent prayer.
Listen carefully. “If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of the LORD thy God” ([[Exod.15.26|Exodus 15:26]]).

modern: This literal promise to Israel belongs spiritually to the children of the Spirit, that is, to all believers. If we live up to our privileges, we’ll live for God so clearly and plainly that people will see we’re set apart for holy service and will call us the priests of the Lord. We may work or do business like everyone else, and yet be solely and wholly God’s ministering servants. Our one occupation will be to offer the never-ending sacrifice of prayer and praise and testimony and self-giving to the living God through Jesus Christ.

Since this is our one aim, we can leave distracting concerns to those who have no higher calling. “Let the dead bury their dead.” It’s written, “Strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of the alien shall be your plowmen and your vine-dressers.” Let them run politics, puzzle out financial problems, discuss science and settle the latest quibbles of the critics. We’ll give ourselves to the kind of service that suits those who, like the Lord Jesus, are appointed to a never-ending priesthood.
Accepting this honorable promise as carrying a sacred duty, let’s put on the robes of holiness and serve before the Lord all day long.

notes.note: Those born of God’s Spirit, the spiritual children of Abraham ([[Gal.3.29|Galatians 3:29]]).
Believers are “an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices” ([[1Pet.2.5|1 Peter 2:5]]).
A never-ending offering. “Let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually” ([[Heb.13.15|Hebrews 13:15]]).
Giving yourself over to God.
[[Matt.8.22|Matthew 8:22]].
[[Isa.61.5|Isaiah 61:5]], the verse before the day’s text. “Alien” means foreigner.
Fine points argued by scholars who studied the Bible skeptically, a hot topic in Spurgeon’s day.
Robes.

modern: Truth wears well. Time tests it, but it stands the test very well. So if I’ve spoken the truth and have to suffer for it for now, I must be content to wait. And if I believe God’s truth and try to declare it, I may meet a lot of opposition, but I don’t need to be afraid, because in the end the truth must win.

What a poor thing the passing triumph of a lie is! “A lying lip is but for a moment!” It’s a mere gourd that comes up in a night and dies in a night, and the bigger it grows, the plainer its decay. On the other hand, how worthy of an undying being it is to stand up for and defend the truth that can never change, the everlasting gospel, which rests on the unchanging truth of an unchanging God! An old proverb says, “He that speaks truth shames the devil.” Certainly whoever speaks the truth of God will put all the devils in hell to shame, and confound all the offspring of the serpent who now hiss out their lies.
My heart, take care to be on the side of truth in everything, in small things and in great, but above all on the side of the One through whom grace and truth have come to us!

notes.term: “A lying lip is but for a moment!”
notes.note: Spurgeon’s wording of the day’s text, which reads “a lying tongue is but for a moment.”
Like Jonah’s plant, which grew up overnight and withered the next day ([[Jonah.4.10|Jonah 4:10]]).
Plain, obvious.
Open declaration.
Unchanging.

notes.term: “He that speaks truth shames the devil”
notes.note: An old proverb, usually “Speak the truth and shame the devil.”
Those who side with the devil ([[Gen.3.15|Genesis 3:15]]).
“Grace and truth came by Jesus Christ” ([[John.1.17|John 1:17]]).

modern: Suspense is dreadful. When we have no news from home, we tend to grow anxious, and we can’t be persuaded that “no news is good news.” Faith is the cure for this sad condition. By his Spirit the Lord settles the mind in holy calm, and all fear is gone, about the future as well as the present.

The steady heart the psalmist speaks of is something to seek earnestly. It isn’t believing this or that promise of the Lord, but a settled state of unshaken trust in our God: the confidence we have in him that he’ll never do us harm himself, or let anyone else harm us. This constant confidence faces the unknown in life as well as the known. Let tomorrow be what it may; our God is the God of tomorrow. Whatever may have happened that we don’t know about yet, our Lord is God of the unknown as well as the known. We’re determined to trust the Lord, come what may. If the very worst should happen, our God is still the greatest and best. So we won’t be afraid, even if the mailman’s knock startles us or a telegram wakes us at midnight. The Lord lives, and what can his children fear?

notes.note: Bad news.
Settled, steady, not shaken.
Steady, not wavering. Abraham “staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief” ([[Rom.4.20|Romans 4:20]]).
Allow.
Tomorrow.
A message sent by electric wire and delivered by hand, in Spurgeon’s day usually urgent and often bad news.

modern: This is good. Our wealth here is very flimsy; there’s no substance to it. But God has given us a promise of real estate in the land of glory, and that promise comes to our hearts with such full assurance that we know in ourselves that we have a lasting substance there. Yes, “we have” it even now. They say, “A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush,” but we have our bird in the bush and in the hand too. Heaven is our own even now. We have the title deed to it. We have the down payment on it. We have the first fruits of it. We have heaven in its price, in its promise and in its principle. And we know this not only by hearing about it, but “in ourselves.”

Shouldn’t the thought of the better substance on the other side of Jordan make us accept our present losses? We may lose our spending money, but our treasure is safe. We’ve lost the shadows, but the substance remains, because our Savior lives, and the place he has prepared for us remains. There’s a better land, a better substance, a better promise, and all of it comes to us by a better covenant. So let’s be in better spirits and say to the Lord, “Every day will I bless thee; and praise thy name for ever and ever.”

notes.note: Property, wealth; also what is real and solid, as opposed to a shadow. Spurgeon plays on both meanings.
The legal document proving you own a property.
A deposit paid up front to promise the rest will follow.
The first part of the harvest, a pledge that the rest is coming ([[Rom.8.23|Romans 8:23]]).

notes.term: In price, in promise, and in principle
notes.note: Heaven has been paid for by Christ, promised by God, and already begun in us.
Heaven. Israel crossed the Jordan to enter the promised land.

notes.term: The place which He has prepared
notes.note: “I go to prepare a place for you” ([[John.14.2|John 14:2]]).
Christ is “the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises” ([[Heb.8.6|Hebrews 8:6]]).

modern: A devout poet sings:

This day comes only once in four years. Oh, that we could win a fourfold blessing on it! Up to now goodness and mercy have followed us like two guards, day after day, bringing up the rear while grace leads the way in front. And since this out-of-the-way day is one of the days of our life, the two guardian angels will be with us today too: goodness to supply our needs, and mercy to wipe out our sins. These two will go with every step we take today, and every day until days are no more. So let’s serve the Lord on this unusual day with a special giving of our hearts, and sing his praises with more zest and sweetness than ever. Couldn’t we make an unusual offering today to God’s cause, or to the poor? With the inventiveness of love, let’s make this twenty-ninth of February a day to be remembered forever.

notes.note: Light up.
Turn of events; what happens.
Goes at the front, like the vanguard of an army.
These two.
Special, belonging particularly to someone (not odd); here, a day all its own.
Giving yourself over to God.
